before.zh: 1858年6月30日，伦敦。两位早已成名的科学家——莱尔与胡克——联名给林奈学会秘书贝内特写信，随信附上三份材料，收信人和写信人都清楚，这三份材料讲的是同一件事（V-E10、V-E17）。麻烦在于：同一套理论被两个人各自独立想了出来，而两个人都没把它发表出去。功劳算谁的、由谁来定，得有人先拿出个说法。
before.en: London, 30 June 1858. Two scientists already at the height of their fame - Charles Lyell and Joseph Dalton Hooker - sat down to a joint letter to J. J. Bennett, secretary of the Linnean Society, the learned body before whose meetings naturalists in Britain read their papers aloud. Three sets of material went with it, and senders and recipient alike knew that all three told one story (V-E10, V-E17, V-E2). The difficulty was plain to state and awkward to resolve: the same theory had occurred to two men working independently of each other, and neither had published. Whose achievement was it, and who had the standing to say so? Someone had to put a version of events on paper first.

after.zh: 1858年6月30日，伦敦。两位皇家学会会员莱尔与胡克联名给林奈学会秘书贝内特写信，随信附上几份材料；信里说，这些材料都关于同一个主题。麻烦在于：同一套理论被两个人各自独立想了出来，而两个人都没把它发表出去。功劳算谁的、由谁来定，得有人先拿出个说法。
after.en: London, 30 June 1858. Charles Lyell and Joseph Dalton Hooker, both Fellows of the Royal Society, wrote a joint letter to J. J. Bennett, secretary of the Linnean Society, enclosing papers which, they said, "all relate to the same subject". The difficulty was plain to state and awkward to resolve: the same theory had occurred to two men working independently of each other, and neither had published. Whose achievement was it, and who had the standing to say so? Someone had to put a version of events on paper first.

before.zh: 先把两位当事人摆出来。达尔文这边，有一份关于物种的手稿：1839年草拟，1844年誊写，胡克在1844年读过誊本，内容后来又告诉了莱尔（V-E3）。多年里，莱尔和胡克反复催达尔文把观点发表出来，他一直没有（V-E2）。华莱士这边，1854年出发去东印度，在马来群岛一带考察了近八年，研究这些岛屿的动植物和部分新几内亚（V-E9）；更早的1848年，他与贝茨同赴巴西，走亚马逊和内格罗河的原始森林，1852年返英，随船的收藏在海难中大半损失（V-E18）。1877年的一篇人物小传记下关键的一句：他在马来群岛研究时并不知道达尔文在同一方向上的先前工作，却得出了几乎相同的结论（V-E8）。
before.en: Begin with the two men themselves. Darwin had a manuscript on species: drafted in 1839, copied out in 1844. Hooker read that copy in 1844, and its contents later reached Lyell (V-E3). For years the two of them pressed Darwin to publish his views; for years he held back (V-E2). Wallace, meanwhile, was travelling. He set out for the East Indies in 1854 and spent nearly eight years exploring the islands of the Malay Archipelago and parts of Papua, studying their animals and plants (V-E9). Earlier, in 1848, he had gone to Brazil with Bates, through the primeval forests of the Amazon and the Rio Negro, and returned to England in 1852; the collections he brought home, especially rich in birds and plants, were largely destroyed by shipwreck (V-E18). A sketch published in 1877 supplies the decisive sentence: while pursuing his researches in the Malay Archipelago, Wallace was unaware of Darwin's earlier labours in the same direction, yet arrived at almost the same general conclusions (V-E8).

before.zh: 于是问题不是谁对，而是两个人各自独立做出同一件事时，功劳怎么分、由谁来分。在1858年的英国科学界，这件事必须落到纸面上：谁署名、谁先讲、由哪个机构讲、按什么顺序讲。莱尔和胡克选择由自己出面安排，并把理由写进一封公开发表的信里。
before.en: So the question was never who was right. It was what to do when two people have independently done the same thing: how credit gets divided, and who divides it. In the scientific world of 1858 that had to be settled on paper - whose name went on the work, who spoke first, through which institution, and in what order. Lyell and Hooker chose to arrange the matter themselves, and to write their reasoning into a letter made for publication.

before.zh: 达尔文的那份旧手稿有点尴尬：它从没打算给人看。1858年，达尔文在手稿前加了一条脚注：「This MS. work was never intended for publication, and therefore was not written with care.—C. D. 1858.」（V-E12），意思是这份手稿从未打算发表，因此写得并不仔细。一位被催促了多年的人，手里一直攥着一份自己都觉得拿不出手的文字。
before.en: Darwin's old manuscript was awkward in a particular way: it had never been meant for other eyes. In 1858 he prefaced it with a footnote - "This MS. work was never intended for publication, and therefore was not written with care.—C. D. 1858." (V-E12) - meaning that he never intended to publish it, and so never wrote it carefully. Here was a man pressed for years to make his views public, holding all the while a text he thought unfit to show anyone.

before.zh: 为了证明他的观点确实早于眼下，莱尔和胡克选了第二份材料：达尔文1857年写给美国波士顿植物学家阿萨·格雷的一封私人信的摘要，信中重申了他的看法，说明这些看法从1839年到1857年没有改变（V-E4）。
before.en: To show that his ideas really did predate the present moment, Lyell and Hookre chose a second item: an abstract of a private letter Darwin had written in October 1857 to Asa Gray, a botanist in Boston, in the United States, in which he restated his views and which showed that they had not changed between 1839 and 1857 (V-E4).

before.zh: 这里有一处材料对不上，照实说：莱尔和胡克的信把这封信写作1857年10月（V-E4），而这份摘要自己的标题写的是1857年9月5日于唐恩（V-E11）。两说并存，证据里没有更多材料可以判谁对，本文也不替它们裁决。
before.en: One detail does not match, and is best reported as it stands. Lyell and Hooker's letter dates this letter October 1857 (V-E4), while the abstract's own heading gives 5 September 1857, at Down (V-E11). Both datings stand in the record; nothing further in the evidence decides between them, and this article does not settle it.

before.zh: 第三份材料是华莱士的论文，标题《论变种无限偏离原初类型的倾向》，落款特尔纳特，1858年2月（V-E13、V-E14）。它是写给朋友兼通信者达尔文看的，作者明确表示：如果达尔文认为它足够新颖、有意思，就请转给莱尔（V-E5）。三份材料按日期排开，像两条互不知情的平行线。达尔文的摘录开头从德堪多和马尔萨斯讲起：「De Candolle, in an eloquent passage, has declared that all nature is at war, one organism with another, or with external nature.」（V-E15）；华莱士则从一条反对意见讲起——家养变种不稳定，常有回归亲本的倾向，因此有人认为物种界限永恒（V-E16）。出发点不同，落点接近。
before.en: The third item was Wallace's essay, "On the Tendency of Varieties to depart indefinitely from the Original Type," dated Ternate, February 1858 (V-E13, V-E14). It was written for his friend and correspondent Darwin to read, with the express wish that, "if Mr. Darwin thought it sufficiently novel and interesting," it should be forwarded to Lyell (V-E5). Laid out by date, the three items look like two parallel lines that never knew of each other. Darwin's extract opens from De Candolle and Malthus: "De Candolle, in an eloquent passage, has declared that all nature is at war, one organism with another, or with external nature." (V-E15), and its next breath calls the struggle "the doctrine of Malthus applied in most cases with tenfold force." Wallace opens from an objection - that domestic varieties are unstable and tend to revert to the parent form, which is taken to show that species were created distinct and are kept that way (V-E16). Different starting points, converging destinations.

before.zh: 达尔文收到论文后的做法，莱尔和胡克写得很具体：他写信给莱尔，提议征得华莱士本人同意后，尽快把这篇论文发表（V-E6）。两位中间人表示赞成，但附了一个条件——达尔文不要像他「as he was strongly inclined to do (in favour of Mr. Wallace)」那样，为照顾华莱士而扣下自己的手稿（V-E6）。原文记下了达尔文的想法：他倾向于把发表的机会让给对方。
before.en: What Darwin did on receiving the essay, Lyell and Hooker describe precisely. He wrote to Lyell proposing to obtain Wallace's consent and have the essay published as soon as possible (V-E6). The two intermediaries approved - with one condition: that Darwin must not withhold his own memoir on the same subject, "as he was strongly inclined to do (in favour of Mr. Wallace)" (V-E6). The wording catches his state of mind: he was inclined to stand aside and leave the field to the other man.

before.zh: 莱尔和胡克向达尔文说明了这样做的理由，达尔文随即同意由他们自行处置他的手稿（V-E7）。他们写下的理由不止是替两人分先后：「we are not solely considering the relative claims to priority of himself and his friend, but the interests of science generally」（V-E7）——不只考虑他与他的朋友谁更早，而是科学的整体利益。他们又补了一句实在话：科学界正等着达尔文的完整著作，与其空等，不如先把他多年劳作的一些主要结果，连同那位能干的通信者的结果，一起摆到公众面前，让别人立刻有一个可以出发的点。
before.en: Lyell and Hooker put their reasoning to Darwin, and he promptly gave them permission to make what use they thought proper of his memoir (V-E7). Their grounds went beyond ranking two men: "we are not solely considering the relative claims to priority of himself and his friend, but the interests of science generally" (V-E7). Then a plain practical point. The scientific world was waiting for Darwin's complete work; better that some of the leading results of his years of labour should be laid before the public now, together with those of his able correspondent, and at once constitute "a goal from which others may start."

before.zh: 1858年7月1日，林奈学会宣读了这批材料（V-E1）。顺序按时间：1839年草拟、1844年誊写的手稿摘录，1857年致格雷信的摘要，最后是华莱士1858年2月的论文（V-E3、V-E4、V-E5）。十九年后那篇小传对此的记述是：华莱士的论文经莱尔转交林奈学会，1858年7月1日宣读，与达尔文的论文同场（V-E19）。
before.en: On 1 July 1858 the material was read to the Linnean Society (V-E1), in chronological order: extracts from the manuscript drafted in 1839 and copied in 1844, then the abstract of the 1857 letter to Gray, and last Wallace's essay of February 1858 (V-E3, V-E4, V-E5). Nineteen years later the sketch of Wallace recorded that his essay, transmitted through Sir Charles Lyell to the Linnean Society, "was read before that body on July 1, 1858, coincidently with the reading of Mr, Darwin's paper" - the sketch gives the title as "On the Tendency of Species to form Varieties, and on the Perpetuation of Species and Varieties by means of Natural Selection" (V-E19).

before.zh: 小传还顺笔记下华莱士后来的路：1862年回英国，此后多年整理他庞大的收藏——十万余件昆虫标本、八千多只鸟（V-E21）；1868年获皇家学会奖章，1870年获巴黎地理学会金质奖章（V-E22）。而在人类起源问题上，他不接受达尔文的结论，认为单靠自然选择不足以完成从猿到人的过渡，还需某种更高原因的共同作用（V-E20）。被写进共同发现者这个位置的人，后来并没有因此变成附议者。
before.en: The sketch also follows Wallace's later course. He returned to England in 1862 and spent several years classifying an enormous collection - upward of 100,000 insect specimens and more than 8,000 birds (V-E21). In 1868 the Royal Society gave him its royal medal; in 1870 the Geographical Society of Paris its gold medal, and in that same year he published "Contributions to the Theory of Natural Selection" (V-E22). On human origins he still would not follow Darwin: natural selection alone, he held, was not competent to effect the transition from the anthropoid apes to man without the joint agency of some higher cause (V-E20). The man placed in the position of co-discoverer did not turn into a yes-man because of it.

In 1868 the Royal Society gave him its royal medal; in 1870 the Geographical Society of Paris its gold medal, and in that same year he published "Contributions to the Theory of Natural Selection". On human origins he still would not follow Darwin: natural selection alone, he held, was not competent to effect the transition from the anthropoid apes to man without the joint agency of some higher cause. The author's view: the man placed in the position of co-discoverer did not become a follower because of it.

before.zh: 一种解释是：莱尔和胡克这套安排，实质上是把功劳归属从两个人之间的争议，改写成一个程序问题。他们能拿得出手的依据有三样：公开的文本、可查的日期、两位彼此独立又与双方相熟的中间人作证。达尔文的旧手稿和致格雷的信摘要证明他想得早，华莱士的论文、落款与寄送方式证明他独立，并且是自己交出来的。作者推断，他们之所以特意强调两人互不知情、且都没发表，正是因为在谁先想到之外，还有一个更难回答的问题：想到而不发表，算不算占住了位置。
before.en: One reading of the arrangement is this: Lyell and Hooker rewrote a dispute between two men over credit as a question of procedure. What they could put on the table was of three kinds - public texts, dates that could be checked, and two intermediaries who were independent of both parties and knew both. Darwin's old manuscript and the abstract of the Gray letter showed how early he had reached the idea; Wallace's essay, with its dateline and the manner of its sending, showed that he had reached it independently and had handed it over himself. The author's inference: they stressed so heavily that the two men did not know of each other's work and that neither had published, because beyond who thought of it first there sits a harder question - whether thinking of something and never publishing is enough to hold your place.

before.zh: 他们给出的回答是：算，但要公开兑现。作者提出的替代做法至少有三种，各有代价：由达尔文先单独发表；只发华莱士，把达尔文的优先权留给他日后自述；或者都等达尔文的完整著作出来再说。列在这里作对照的是作者提出的选项，不是材料里的记载。实际被选中的是第四条：三份材料同场宣读，日期写进正文，理由写给一位秘书并公开发表。莱尔和胡克自己说，这样做的依据是让经年思考、建立在大量事实上的观点立刻成为别人可以出发的目标（V-E7）。分配交给了程序，而不是交给任何一位当事人的谦让。
before.en: Their answer was: yes, but it has to be cashed in publicly. The author sets out at least three alternative courses, each with its own price: Darwin publishing alone first; only Wallace published, with Darwin left to state his own priority later; or everyone waiting for Darwin's complete book. What is listed here for contrast are options constructed by the author, not episodes recorded in the documents. The course actually taken was a fourth: three sets of material read together in one session, the dates printed in the body of the text, the reasoning addressed to a secretary and made public. The warrant Lyell and Hooker gave was that views founded on a wide deduction from facts and matured by years of reflection should at once become a goal from which others might start (V-E7). The allocation was handed to a procedure, not to the generosity of either party.

before.zh: 现代虚构场景一：一家公司里两个互不通气的小组，各自做出了相似的推荐算法，都想报专利。两边负责人都愿意让一让，专利代理人却说，让不让不由他们决定，得看谁先留下的记录能被第三方核对。
before.en: A modern fictional scene, first. Two teams inside one company, which have never compared notes, build similar recommendation algorithms, and both want to file for a patent. Both team leads are willing to give ground. The patent attorney tells them that giving ground is not theirs to decide: what counts is which of them left records that a third party can verify.

before.zh: 现代虚构场景二：一位中学老师把实验设计发在自己的公众号上，一位研究生几乎同时写成论文投稿。两人都不想争，编辑说他不能替他们判定谁算原创，只能请双方各交材料、写清时间线，再请一位双方都认的同行来安排刊出方式。
before.en: A modern fictional scene, second. A secondary-school teacher puts an experimental design on her own public account, and a graduate student writes up nearly the same design and submits it almost at the same time. Neither wants a fight. The editor says he cannot pronounce on who counts as original. He can only ask both sides for their material and a clear timeline, then invite a peer both accept to arrange how the work appears in print.

after.zh: 现代虚构场景一：一位研究员的一篇方法草稿在硬盘里放了三年，同事一再催她投出去，她总觉得还不够好。某天，她在预印本网站上看到别人刚发了几乎一样的方法。这时候能拿出来的，只有草稿的版本记录，以及那几位早年读过草稿的同事愿不愿意写下他们看到过什么。
after.en: Fictional modern scene one. A researcher has kept a draft of a method on her hard drive for three years; colleagues keep urging her to submit it, and she keeps feeling it is not ready. One day she finds almost the same method in a preprint someone has just posted. What she can produce now is the version history of her draft, and whether the colleagues who read it years ago are willing to put in writing what they saw.

before.zh: 本文依据的记录有两类，都要打折看。一类是莱尔和胡克1858年6月30日给林奈学会秘书的说明信，他们是安排的当事人，也是作证人；另一类是1877年《大众科学月刊》上的一篇人物小传，动笔时距1858年已近二十年。手头没有达尔文、华莱士本人的书信，所以本文不写他们的心情，不写他们当场的反应，也不写两人私下如何商量。
before.en: The records this article rests on fall into two classes, and both deserve a discount. One is the explanatory letter Lyell and Hooker wrote to the secretary of the Linnean Society on 30 June 1858; they were at once parties to the arrangement and witnesses to it. The other is a personal sketch in Popular Science Monthly from 1877, written nearly twenty years after the event. With no letters of Darwin's or Wallace's in hand, this article does not write about their feelings, their reactions at the time, or how the two of them settled matters between themselves.

before.zh: 同样，证据包没有说明华莱士在宣读之前是否知情、是否同意，这一点本文不作任何陈述。致格雷信的日期两说并存，照原样保留。至于这次宣读之后的事，包括达尔文后来的著作如何问世，不在本文范围内。可以确定的只有这次安排本身：三份材料、一位收信人、一个日期，以及写在信上的理由。
before.en: Likewise, the evidence does not say whether Wallace knew of the reading beforehand or consented to it, and this article makes no statement either way. The date of the letter to Gray stands in two versions and is left as found. What followed 1 July 1858, including how Darwin's later books reached the world, lies outside the scope here. What can be fixed is the arrangement itself: three sets of material, one addressee, one date, and the reasons written into the letter.
